title: A new 532-nm picosecond Nd:YAG laser matched an established system for freckles: an 84-person split-face noninferiority trial
headline: Both lasers cleared freckles equally (response 97.6% each) after one session in Chinese patients; it tests equivalence of two devices, not whether either is safe or useful for melasma or post-inflammatory pigment in deeper skin.
evidenceTier: Randomized split-face noninferiority trial, 84 people; abstract read; full text not opened
fit: A cost and access story about device makers, not a skin-of-colour pigment result. Freckles are a different problem from melasma and PIH.
displaces: Fits nowhere; relevant only when choosing between clinics' devices for freckles.
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
summaryPoints: Abstract (read): randomized, evaluator-blinded split-face, one session, 84 participants; response rate at 8 weeks 97.6% vs 97.6% (difference 0.0%, 95% CI -3.3% to 3.3%); cure rates 13.1% vs 9.5% (p=.53); participant satisfaction 72.6% vs 58.3% (p=.001). No serious adverse events.
Skin type is not given in the abstract (MeSH term East Asian People); the 8-week follow-up cannot speak to rebound or pigment loss; 'cure' rates were low for both.
Verdict is SKIP for this reader because the question answered (is a new device as good as an old one for freckles) does not touch melasma, PIH or Fitzpatrick V to VI.
toneData: East Asian participants (Fitzpatrick type not in abstract)
fitLine: Device-equivalence result for a different pigment condition, not tested in deeper skin.
